subject.title: [Regression]: sessions_spawn missing scope operator.write — introduced between v2026.6.1 and v2026.6.11

question: Should non-admin in-process `callSubagentGateway` `agent` dispatch use a synthetic `operator.write` client after `sessions_spawn` tool policy authorizes the spawn?
rationale: The narrow fix appears to solve the source-reproducible regression, but it deliberately changes an internal Gateway authorization boundary from inherited channel/plugin scopes to a synthetic write-scoped client.

options.title: Accept Narrow Synthetic Boundary
options.body: Land PR 99199 or equivalent after redacted token-auth channel proof confirms the spawn path works and cleanup remains admin-scoped.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Auth Policy
options.body: Pause this issue behind the wider token-auth/device-identity policy work if maintainers want one canonical Gateway auth solution.

options.title: Keep Inherited Client Boundary
options.body: Reject synthetic write elevation for this path and require a different design that supplies `operator.write` without changing the in-process dispatch boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Synthetic Boundary
recommendation.body: Land PR 99199 or equivalent after redacted token-auth channel proof confirms the spawn path works and cleanup remains admin-scoped.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the in-process dispatch work and authored follow-up commits in the same Gateway dispatch area.
